section.title: org.osgi.service.dmt.security
section.para: Device Management Tree Security Package Version 2.0.
This package contains the permission classes used by the Device Management API in environments that support the Java 2 security model.

Bundles wishing to use this package must list the package in the Import-Package header of the bundle's manifest. This package has two types of users: the consumers that use the API in this package and the providers that implement the API in this package.
Example import for consumers using the API in this package:
{@code Import-Package: org.osgi.service.dmt.security; version="[2.0,3.0)"}
Example import for providers implementing the API in this package:
{@code Import-Package: org.osgi.service.dmt.security; version="[2.0,2.1)"}

listitem.para: AlertPermission - Indicates the callers authority to send alerts to management servers, identified by their principal names.
DmtPermission - Controls access to management objects in the Device Management Tree (DMT).
DmtPrincipalPermission - Indicates the callers authority to create DMT sessions on behalf of a remote management server.

section.title: public class AlertPermission extends Permission
section.para: Indicates the callers authority to send alerts to management servers, identified by their principal names.

{@code AlertPermission} has a target string which controls the principal names where alerts can be sent. A wildcard is allowed at the end of the target string, to allow sending alerts to any principal with a name matching the given prefix. The "*" target means that alerts can be sent to any destination.

section.title: public AlertPermission(String target)

formalpara.title: target
formalpara.para: the name of a principal, can end with {@code *} to match any principal identifier with the given prefix

section.para: Creates a new {@code AlertPermission} object with its name set to the target string. Name must be non-null and non-empty.

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: NullPointerException– if {@code name} is {@code null}

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: IllegalArgumentException– if {@code name} is empty

section.title: public AlertPermission(String target, String actions)

formalpara.title: target
formalpara.para: the name of the server, can end with {@code *} to match any server identifier with the given prefix

formalpara.title: actions
formalpara.para: no actions defined, must be "*" for forward compatibility

section.para: Creates a new {@code AlertPermission} object using the 'canonical' two argument constructor. In this version this class does not define any actions, the second argument of this constructor must be "*" so that this class can later be extended in a backward compatible way.

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: NullPointerException– if {@code name} or {@code actions} is {@code null}

formalpara.title: Throws

section.title: public class DmtPermission extends Permission
section.para: Controls access to management objects in the Device Management Tree (DMT). It is intended to control local access to the DMT. DmtPermission target string identifies the management object URI and the action field lists the OMA DM commands that are permitted on the management object. Example:

This means that owner of this permission can execute Add, Replace and Get commands on the ./OSGi/bundles management object. It is possible to use wildcards in both the target and the actions field. Wildcard in the target field means that the owner of the permission can access children nodes of the target node. Example:

This means that owner of this permission has Get access on every child node of ./OSGi/bundles. The asterisk does not necessarily have to follow a '/' character. For example the {@code "./OSGi/a*"} target matches the {@code ./OSGi/applications} subtree.

If wildcard is present in the actions field, all legal OMA DM commands are allowed on the designated nodes(s) by the owner of the permission. Action names are interpreted case-insensitively, but the canonical action string returned by {@link #getActions()} uses the forms defined by the action constants.

section.title: public static final String ADD = "Add"
section.para: Holders of DmtPermission with the Add action present can create new nodes in the DMT, that is they are authorized to execute the createInteriorNode() and createLeafNode() methods of the DmtSession. This action is also required for the copy() command, which needs to perform node creation operations (among others).

section.title: public static final String DELETE = "Delete"
public static final String EXEC = "Exec"
section.para: Holders of DmtPermission with the Exec action present can execute nodes in the DMT, that is they are authorized to call the execute() method of the DmtSession.

section.title: public static final String GET = "Get"
section.para: Holders of DmtPermission with the Get action present can query DMT node value or properties, that is they are authorized to execute the isLeafNode(), getNodeAcl(), getEffectiveNodeAcl(), getMetaNode(), getNodeValue(), getChildNodeNames(), getNodeTitle(), getNodeVersion(), getNodeTimeStamp(), getNodeSize() and getNodeType() methods of the DmtSession. This action is also required for the copy() command, which needs to perform node query operations (among others).

section.title: public static final String REPLACE = "Replace"
section.para: Holders of DmtPermission with the Replace action present can update DMT node value or properties, that is they are authorized to execute the setNodeAcl(), setNodeTitle(), setNodeValue(), setNodeType() and renameNode() methods of the DmtSession. This action is also be required for the copy() command if the original node had a title property (which must be set in the new node).

section.title: public DmtPermission(String dmtUri, String actions)

formalpara.title: dmtUri
formalpara.para: URI of the management object (or subtree)

formalpara.title: actions
formalpara.para: OMA DM actions allowed

section.para: Creates a new DmtPermission object for the specified DMT URI with the specified actions. The given URI can be:

listitem.para: {@code "*"}, which matches all valid (see {@link Uri#isValidUri(String)}) absolute URIs;
a valid absolute URI, which matches itself.

section.para: Since the {@code *} character is itself a valid URI character, it can appear as the last character of a valid absolute URI. To distinguish this case from using {@code *} as a wildcard, the {@code *} character at the end of the URI must be escaped with the {@code \} character. For example the URI {@code "./a*"} matches {@code "./a"}, {@code "./aa"}, {@code "./a/b"} etc. while {@code "./a\*"} matches {@code "./a*"} only.
The actions string must either be "*" to allow all actions, or it must contain a non-empty subset of the valid actions, defined as constants in this class.

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: NullPointerException– if any of the parameters are {@code null}

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: IllegalArgumentException– if any of the parameters are invalid

section.title: public boolean equals(Object obj)

formalpara.title: obj
formalpara.para: the object to compare to this DmtPermission instance

section.para: Checks whether the given object is equal to this DmtPermission instance. Two DmtPermission instances are equal if they have the same target string and the same action mask. The "*" action mask is considered equal to a mask containing all actions.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: {@code true} if the parameter represents the same permissions as this instance

section.title: public String getActions()
section.para: Returns the String representation of the action list. The allowed actions are listed in the following order: Add, Delete, Exec, Get, Replace. The wildcard character is not used in the returned string, even if the class was created using the "*" wildcard.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: canonical action list for this permission object

section.title: public int hashCode()
section.para: Returns the hash code for this permission object. If two DmtPermission objects are equal according to the {@link #equals(Object)} method, then calling this method on each of the two DmtPermission objects must produce the same integer result.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: hash code for this permission object

section.title: public boolean implies(Permission p)

formalpara.title: p
formalpara.para: the permission to check for implication

section.para: Checks if this DmtPermission object "implies" the specified permission. This method returns {@code false} if and only if at least one of the following conditions are fulfilled for the specified permission:

listitem.para: its set of actions contains an action not allowed by this permission
the set of nodes defined by its path contains a node not defined by the path of this permission

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: true if this DmtPermission instance implies the specified permission

section.title: public PermissionCollection newPermissionCollection()
section.para: Returns a new PermissionCollection object for storing DmtPermission objects.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: the new PermissionCollection

section.title: public class DmtPrincipalPermission extends Permission
section.para: Indicates the callers authority to create DMT sessions on behalf of a remote management server. Only protocol adapters communicating with management servers should be granted this permission.

{@code DmtPrincipalPermission} has a target string which controls the name of the principal on whose behalf the protocol adapter can act. A wildcard is allowed at the end of the target string, to allow using any principal name with the given prefix. The "*" target means the adapter can create a session in the name of any principal.
